title: Durable replica repair and topology reconciliation
summary: Provider and topology transitions are committed by Storage authority first, then affected StorageRefs are re-assessed against current replica policy. Real deficits become durable Queue Fabric repair work; replayed or stale work re-assesses before copying, so repair is idempotent and safety remains a Storage decision rather than a telemetry or transport inference.
invariants: TEMPORARY is lifecycle/purpose; DISPOSABLE is explicit data-loss authority. Never infer DISPOSABLE from a temporary path, scratch role, cache label or short retention.
OFFLINE or unreachable is not LOST. Known replica identity and prior verification evidence may remain while the location does not count toward current effective protection.
Provider/topology state is committed by Storage authority before repair reconciliation observes it.
Every committed topology transition may trigger re-assessment of only the Storage objects associated with the affected provider.
Repair work is created only when current StorageReplicaPolicy assessment is unsatisfied.
StorageReplicaRequirement uses requiredReplicas, distinctVendors, distinctSites and distinctFailureDomains; adapters must not invent alternate field names.
Queue Fabric owns durable delivery, CLAIM/ACK/NACK and crash recovery; Storage owns replica policy, destination eligibility, copy, independent verification and admission.
A stale or duplicate repair request must re-resolve the StorageRef and re-assess current policy before movement; an already-protected object completes as a successful no-op.
Instrumentation Mesh reports repair and provider transitions but never makes an object safe, admits a replica or authorises loss.
Placement preference is independent of durability policy. A fibre-connected laptop USB, Git/Azure provider or cloud volume may be preferred when eligible; provider fashion is not placement authority.
Git push/commit success is not replica admission. Remote commit/ref and object/chunk identity must be independently verified before the Git location counts as AVAILABLE/VERIFIED/SAFE.
FUSE is a projection surface. Authority persistence, replica evidence and repair state remain below FUSE and survive surface restart independently.
procedure: Commit the provider/location transition in Storage authority.
Find catalogue objects associated with the affected provider.
Resolve each object's current persisted StorageReplicaRequirement.
Assess current AVAILABLE, VERIFIED and SAFE eligible locations and required diversity.
For unsatisfied objects, submit deterministic persistent STORAGE.REPAIR work to the existing ObjectQueueManager.
On CLAIM, re-resolve object and policy; no-op if protection has already been restored.
Choose an eligible destination through placement policy, then copy, independently verify and admit the new location.
Re-assess current policy; ACK only after protection is satisfied, otherwise NACK/retry according to Queue Fabric policy.
Publish bounded Instrumentation Mesh repair/progress observations only after the corresponding authoritative transition succeeds.

provenance.claim: StorageReplicaRequirement and StorageReplicaPolicy API grounding for repair reconciliation.
Dev23-compatible durable repair payload and post-commit provider/topology reconciliation implementation; static qualification only in this environment.

qualification_boundary: The dev5 adapter static contract tests passed in the packaging environment. No ooRexx runtime execution, live Queue Fabric CLAIM/ACK adapter qualification, live Azure Git operation, or live removable-provider transition is claimed by this continuation article.
